subject: Request: One-off SLA offset for BrightHealth — regional failover timeline
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Benito <sarah.benito@brighthealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: One-off SLA offset for BrightHealth — regional failover timeline

Hi Sarah / BrightHealth team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We heard you loud and clear: the absence of multi-region failover in the private deployment has increased your outage exposure during maintenance windows, and that materially impacted two of your pilot environments last month. We own that gap.

Internal ask (cc’ing product & leadership): before I send an official amendment to BrightHealth, I need an internal decision on a one-off commercial offset to bridge until regional failover ships. Proposal options (quick):
- Option A: 20% credit on Sep–Oct invoices (2 months), capped at $25k
- Option B: Usage credit equal to 25% of estimated error-hours cost, up to $40k, conditional on renewed 12-month commitment

Attached: draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP), SLA-offset calc.

If we agree, I’ll send a short amendment and a DocuSign to contracts. Can product confirm a realistic ship date so we can tie any credit to a firm ETA?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: BrightHealth_MAP_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA-offset-calc-09-07.pdf (calc)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: One-off SLA offset for BrightHealth — regional failover timeline

Alex — thanks for drafting. A few asks before we commit:
1) Can product (Priyom) confirm the ETA and whether the ship is gated on any third-party infra? Need a date we can promise publicly.
2) Finance: what’s our approval threshold for credits without C-level sign-off? If this is >$30k we may need an exec approval.
3) Legal: any standard language we should include to avoid setting a precedent?

Happy to approve a customer-facing amount up to $20k from sales discretionary; beyond that I’ll need an OK from Vivek/finance. Priyom — tagging you for ETA + technical mitigation note.

- Laura
VP, Commercial Operations

Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: One-off SLA offset for BrightHealth — regional failover timeline

Alex / team — product update and clarifications:
- Root cause: the regional failover work requires an infra dependency (regional routing layer) that we originally scoped for Q3; that dependency slipped due to vendor cert testing.
- New ETA: feature code complete 2026-11-20, QA + compliance 2026-12-15. Targeting a limited private roll in late Dec.
- Mitigation: we can provide a standby routing policy and manual DR runbooks for BrightHealth starting immediately (no code changes). That reduces outage surface but is operationally heavier.

Suggested commercial structure aligned to ETA: 10% credit for Sep–Nov (3 months) capped at $30k, plus a one-time professional services package to run DR drills in Oct for $12k (discounted to $6k if included). Conditional on renewal discussion by Nov 15.

Attached: product-failover-roadmap-note.pdf (internal note).

Priyom
Senior PM, Platform

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed accommodation and next steps — BrightHealth private deployment

Sarah / Contracts team — thanks for your patience while we pulled internal alignment. Here’s a proposal to bridge to regional failover availability:
1) Commercial accommodation: 10% credit on invoices for Sep–Nov 2026 (3 months), capped at $30,000.
2) Operational support: two DR drills run by Redwood PS in October (discounted rate of $6,000).
3) Roadmap commitment: target ship date for private regional failover is 2026-12-15; we’ll include this ETA in the MAP and monitor progress jointly.

If BrightHealth is comfortable with the above, we will prepare a short amendment to the Master Subscription Agreement and route via DocuSign. The credit is conditional on executing the MAP and on agreeing to a renewal discussion by Nov 15, 2026.

Attachments: BrightHealth_MAP_draft.xlsx, SLA-offset-calc-09-07.pdf

Next steps for internal approvers: please confirm final sign-off (legal & finance) so I can send the amendment to Contracts.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed accommodation and next steps — BrightHealth private deployment

Team — legal and finance reviewed. We can approve the 10% / $30k accommodation with the following redlines:
- Credit must appear as a line-item credit on the invoice with an internal chase code.
- MAP must include the explicit ETA (2026-12-15) and an acceptance test definition for the private regional failover.
- Include one-time non-precedent language: "This accommodation is a one-time, non-precedent commercial concession tied specifically to BrightHealth Contract DL-2026-0874."

I have attached a redlined amendment (SLA-amendment-redline.docx) and opened a DocuSign envelope template for Alex to send once you confirm acceptance. Vivek — recommend recording the approval in the executive approval tracker.

Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations & Legal Liaison
Attachments: SLA-amendment-redline.docx; DocuSign envelope ID: DS-77-2026 (link sent internally)
